rows.note: Use this for the right to enter or leave a physical place, rather than for digital permissions or connectivity.

example.english: You need access to this venue before you can go in.
example.traditional: 呢個場地要有出入權先入得去。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 coeng4 dei6 jiu3 jau5 ceot1 jap6 kyun4 sin1 jap6 dak1 heoi3

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose colloquial choice when you mean being able to get or access the data.

example.english: I can access the file now.
example.jyutping: ngo5 ji4 gaa1 lo2 dou3 go3 dong2 on3 laa3

rows.note: Use this when access specifically means being able to view or read the data.

example.english: You can access the report after logging in.
example.traditional: 你登入之後就睇到份報告。
example.jyutping: nei5 dang1 jap6 zi1 hau6 zau6 tai2 dou2 fan6 bou3 gou3

rows.note: Use this technical computing verb when access includes retrieving or manipulating stored data rather than merely viewing it.

example.english: This program can access the data on the server.
example.traditional: 呢個程式可以存取伺服器入面嘅資料。
example.jyutping: ni1 go3 cing4 sik1 ho2 ji5 cyun4 ceoi2 si6 fuk6 hei3 jap6 min6 ge3 zi1 liu2

rows.note: Use this for access understood as a computer or Internet connection, rather than permission to use a system.

example.english: The company has no access to the network right now.
example.jyutping: gung1 si1 ji4 gaa1 mou5 mong5 lok6 lin4 sin3

rows.note: Use this for permission to access or use a computer system, program, or online resource.

example.english: You don't have access to view this file.
example.jyutping: nei5 mou5 kyun4 haan6 tai2 ni1 fan6 man4 gin6

rows.note: Use this when access means how easy it is to approach, enter, or reach a place or resource.

example.english: This hotel has pretty convenient access to the MTR station.
example.traditional: 呢間酒店去地鐵站嘅方便程度幾高㗎。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 zau2 dim3 heoi3 dei6 tit3 zaam6 ge3 fong1 bin6 cing4 dou6 gei2 gou1 gaa3
